through_line: This week's builds were connective tissue for agents, not new models.
prior_through_lines: Issue 2: Agents are gaining persistent memory and self-composing skill loops between sessions.
Issue 4: This week's breakout repos pulled AI off the cloud and onto hardware the user owns.
evidence_paragraph: Three of the five picks build the same layer from different angles. @jlowin's FastMCP (2026-06-03) shipped v3.4 Remote Control, a bridge that lets stdio-only hosts reach HTTP and SSE MCP servers. @chopra_tejas's headroom (2026-06-04) ships a library, a proxy, and an MCP server that compress what an agent reads by 60 to 95 percent before it hits the model. @D4Vinci1's Scrapling (2026-06-02) carries a built-in MCP server so agents scrape the live web natively. None trained a model. Each one widened what an agent can reach, read, or run.
counter_signal: The surface isn't always open or standardized; @nbushak's boxes.dev is a closed hosted product and @mvanhorn's last30days ships as a portable skill, not a server.
candidate_through_line_for_hero_tiebreak: The agent's reach layer, what it can touch, read, and run on, was the week's main build.
